title: Orchestration wizard for context-aware support actions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight orchestration 'wizard' in the Console that converts runbook steps into idempotent, context-aware tasks operators can run against production clusters. This is a focused effort to reduce human error during support flows by codifying conditional steps, pre-flight checks, and safe roll-forward/rollback actions.

Scope: the first iteration should support: templated variables populated from request context (route, model, cluster, recent traces), built-in pre-checks (SLO/latency, GPU memory headroom, KV-cache hit ratio), dry-run mode (no side-effects, only validation), audit logging tied to customer/route metadata, and a minimal UI to pick a saved runbook, run pre-checks, review diffs, and execute steps. Steps should be stored as small task definitions (shell-safe, API calls, or operator prompts) and be idempotent where possible.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered: 
- Synchronous vs async execution: We will run steps through the existing ops-task queue to allow pacing, retries, and observability rather than performing long-running synchronous HTTP requests from the Console. This adds small latency to visible completion but gains retry semantics and better telemetry.
- DSL complexity: Keep step definition language minimal (YAML with a few verbs: http_call, kubectl, prompt, wait_for_metric) instead of a full DSL to reduce learning curve and security surface.
- Safety by default: Every step will require an explicit confirmation level (suggested/approved/force). Force requires additional 2FA or SSO re-auth when security_review_required=true.
- Side-effect minimization: Default run mode is dry-run and suggestions only. Users must actively switch to execute mode with an explanation of customer impact.

Integrations:
- Console UI: new Wizard view with pre-check run summary and a step-by-step execution log.
- Backend: ops-controller task API (new endpoints described in PR), job metadata includes route_id, request_id, user_email, and reason.
- Audit: events sent to existing audit-log pipeline (Kafka topic: audit.admin-actions) and linked to the Customer Activity view.
- Docs/Playbooks: links to Confluence runbook pages and a canonical examples repo.

Success metrics for the first month after launch: 
- 40% reduction in manual-shell remediation steps for pilot teams.
- 95% of executed steps include pre-check pass/fail metadata.
- No production outages attributable to wizard usage.

Non-goals for v1: full multi-step rollback orchestrator, arbitrary script execution, or replacing the existing runbooks-as-code product (this is an ops-focused UI/flow).
acceptance_criteria: Wizard UI allows selection of a saved runbook and shows a pre-check summary
Pre-checks can be executed in dry-run and return deterministic pass/fail with reasons
Executing a step enqueues an ops-task with metadata and returns a task id visible in the Console
All executions produce audit records with route_id, user_email, and runbook_id
Steps support at least three verbs: http_call, kubectl (restricted namespace list), and prompt
Force-execute requires elevated confirmation (SSO re-auth or 2FA) when marked security_review_required
Telemetry dashboards (errors, avg-step-latency, precheck-pass-rate) are available in Grafana
Documentation page with examples and a migration guide added to Confluence
